```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

```

# Model and source

Back et al. (2019) fitted three independent one-compartment population PK
models to three retrospective Korean paediatric therapeutic-drug-monitoring
datasets, to compare an allometric size function alone with size plus a
sigmoidal maturation function. Each drug is its own model file:

* `Back_2019_cyclosporine`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_cyclosporine"))$description`
* `Back_2019_phenobarbital`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_phenobarbital"))$description`
* `Back_2019_vancomycin`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_vancomycin"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_cyclosporine"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics11060259>

**Read the Errata section before using the phenobarbital or vancomycin model.**
Two of the three published parameter sets do not reproduce the paper's own
visual predictive check. All three are encoded exactly as printed in Table 3.

# Population

All three cohorts are single-centre Korean hospital cohorts (Back 2019 Table 1):

* **Cyclosporine A (CsA)**: 34 infants and children (20 male, 14 female) with
  retinoblastoma at Yonsei University Hospital, postnatal age 26.8 +/- 17.8
  (1-79) months, weight 12.9 +/- 3.8 (5-24) kg. High-dose CsA was infused over
  24 h, starting 3 h before chemotherapy on days 1 and 2, as a P-glycoprotein
  inhibitor; samples were drawn 20 h after the start of each infusion.
* **Phenobarbital (PHB)**: 28 preterm and term neonates and infants (11 male,
  17 female) in the Kyunghee University NICU, gestational age 36.7 +/- 4.4
  weeks, postnatal age 32.4 +/- 30.7 (3-150) days, post-conceptional age
  41.3 +/- 3.9 (31-51.1) weeks, weight 3.3 +/- 1 (1-6.9) kg. Loading dose
  15-20 mg/kg, then 3-5 mg/kg/day from 12-24 h later, oral or intravenous;
  troughs between 5 min and 3 h before the next dose.
* **Vancomycin (VAN)**: 93 preterm neonates to infants (57 male, 36 female) at
  Chungnam National University Hospital, gestational age 31.9 +/- 4.7 weeks,
  postnatal age 9.3 +/- 12.4 (0.1-80.4) weeks, post-conceptional age
  41.2 +/- 14.2 (25.6-110) weeks, weight 3.2 +/- 2.6 (0.4-14.9) kg.
  Weight-based intravenous doses every 6-24 h; samples 0.5-23.5 h after a dose.

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Back_2019_vancomycin")()$population`.

# Source trace

The paper's post-conceptional age (PCA) is gestational age plus postnatal age
(Table 1: 36.7 weeks + 32.4 days = 41.3 weeks), i.e. the standard
postmenstrual age, supplied in the canonical `PAGE` column in **weeks**.

| Equation / parameter | CsA | PHB | VAN | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Structure | 1-cmt IV | 1-cmt, first-order oral absorption + IV | 1-cmt IV | Results 3.2; Figure 1 |
| `Vd = TVVd * (WT/70)^1 * exp(eta)` | yes | yes | yes | Eq 4 and Eq 7; WTnormal = 70 kg (Methods 2.4) |
| `CL = TVCL * (WT/70)^0.75 * Fmat * exp(eta)` | no `Fmat` | yes | yes | Eq 8 (two-branch) |
| `Fmat = PCA^Hill / (PCA^Hill + TM50^Hill)` | -- | yes | yes | Eq 2, Eq 5, Eq 8 |
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg, L/h) | 21.3 | 0.569 | 69.4 | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (Vd at 70 kg, L) | 218 | 5.51 | 3.23 | Table 3 |
| TM50 (weeks) | -- | 48.2 (`ltmat50`) | 33.3, held constant (`tmat50`) | Table 3 and footnote |
| Hill | -- | 5.99 (`lhill_mat`) | 3.68, held constant (`hill_mat`) | Table 3 and footnote |
| `lka` (1/h) | -- | 50, held constant | -- | Table 3 |
| `lfdepot` | -- | 0.724 | -- | Table 3 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 | 0.75, 1 | 0.75, 1 | Eq 7, Eq 8 (printed exponents) |
| IIV CL (CV) -> `etalcl` variance | 16.8% -> 0.02783 | 40.8% -> 0.154 | 10.4% -> 0.01076 | Table 3; `log(CV^2 + 1)` |
| IIV Vd (CV) -> `etalvc` variance | 12.3% -> 0.01502 | 78.7% -> 0.482 | 52.8% -> 0.2459 | Table 3; `log(CV^2 + 1)` |
| `propSd` | 0.468 | 0.356 | 0.408 | Table 3; Eq 6 (CCV model) |

```{r transcription}
ui <- list(
  CsA = rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_cyclosporine")),
  PHB = rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_phenobarbital")),
  VAN = rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Back_2019_vancomycin"))
)
th <- lapply(ui, function(u) u$theta)

# Every structural value against Back 2019 Table 3, on the scale printed there.
table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~param,      ~printed, ~encoded,
  "CsA", "CL (L/h)",  21.3,     exp(th$CsA[["lcl"]]),
  "CsA", "Vd (L)",    218,      exp(th$CsA[["lvc"]]),
  "CsA", "prop err",  0.468,    th$CsA[["propSd"]],
  "PHB", "CL (L/h)",  0.569,    exp(th$PHB[["lcl"]]),
  "PHB", "Vd (L)",    5.51,     exp(th$PHB[["lvc"]]),
  "PHB", "TM50 (wk)", 48.2,     exp(th$PHB[["ltmat50"]]),
  "PHB", "Hill",      5.99,     exp(th$PHB[["lhill_mat"]]),
  "PHB", "ka (1/h)",  50,       exp(th$PHB[["lka"]]),
  "PHB", "F",         0.724,    exp(th$PHB[["lfdepot"]]),
  "PHB", "prop err",  0.356,    th$PHB[["propSd"]],
  "VAN", "CL (L/h)",  69.4,     exp(th$VAN[["lcl"]]),
  "VAN", "Vd (L)",    3.23,     exp(th$VAN[["lvc"]]),
  "VAN", "TM50 (wk)", 33.3,     th$VAN[["tmat50"]],
  "VAN", "Hill",      3.68,     th$VAN[["hill_mat"]],
  "VAN", "prop err",  0.408,    th$VAN[["propSd"]]
)
stopifnot(nrow(table3) == 15L, max(abs(table3$encoded / table3$printed - 1)) < 1e-12)

# IIV: Table 3 CV% converted with omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)
cv_tab <- c(CsA_cl = 16.8, CsA_v = 12.3, PHB_cl = 40.8, PHB_v = 78.7, VAN_cl = 10.4, VAN_v = 52.8)
om <- c(
  CsA_cl = ui$CsA$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"], CsA_v = ui$CsA$omega["etalvc", "etalvc"],
  PHB_cl = ui$PHB$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"], PHB_v = ui$PHB$omega["etalvc", "etalvc"],
  VAN_cl = ui$VAN$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"], VAN_v = ui$VAN$omega["etalvc", "etalvc"]
)
cv_back <- 100 * sqrt(exp(om) - 1)
stopifnot(max(abs(cv_back - cv_tab)) < 0.05)
knitr::kable(table3, digits = 4, caption = "Encoded values against Back 2019 Table 3.")
```

# Typical subjects

The typical subject of each cohort is the Table 1 mean weight and
post-conceptional age. Derived quantities follow directly from Eq 7 and Eq 8.

```{r typical}
typ <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~WT,  ~PAGE,
  "CsA", 12.9, NA_real_,
  "PHB", 3.3,  41.3,
  "VAN", 3.2,  41.2
)
fmat_fun <- function(page, tm50, hill) page^hill / (page^hill + tm50^hill)
typ <- typ |>
  mutate(
    tvcl = c(exp(th$CsA[["lcl"]]), exp(th$PHB[["lcl"]]), exp(th$VAN[["lcl"]])),
    tvv = c(exp(th$CsA[["lvc"]]), exp(th$PHB[["lvc"]]), exp(th$VAN[["lvc"]])),
    fmat = c(1,
             fmat_fun(41.3, exp(th$PHB[["ltmat50"]]), exp(th$PHB[["lhill_mat"]])),
             fmat_fun(41.2, th$VAN[["tmat50"]], th$VAN[["hill_mat"]])),
    cl = tvcl * (WT / 70)^0.75 * fmat,
    v = tvv * (WT / 70),
    cl_per_kg = cl / WT,
    v_per_kg = v / WT,
    thalf_h = log(2) * v / cl
  )
knitr::kable(
  typ |>
    select(drug, WT, PAGE, fmat, cl, v, cl_per_kg, v_per_kg, thalf_h) |>
    rename("Drug" = drug, "WT (kg)" = WT, "PCA (weeks)" = PAGE, "Fmat" = fmat,
           "CL (L/h)" = cl, "Vd (L)" = v, "CL (L/h/kg)" = cl_per_kg,
           "Vd (L/kg)" = v_per_kg, "t1/2 (h)" = thalf_h),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Typical-subject parameters implied by Table 3 and Eq 7-8."
)

# Pinned arithmetic of the printed values: a mis-transcribed CL, Vd, TM50 or
# Hill moves these by far more than the tolerance.
stopifnot(
  abs(typ$thalf_h[typ$drug == "CsA"] / 4.65 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(typ$thalf_h[typ$drug == "PHB"] / 11.0 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(typ$thalf_h[typ$drug == "VAN"] * 60 / 1.30 - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The CsA typical subject (CL 0.46 L/h/kg, Vd 3.1 L/kg, half-life 4.7 h) is
plausible for a child. The phenobarbital Vd of 0.08 L/kg and the vancomycin
half-life of 1.3 minutes are not; see the Errata.

# Self-consistency: rxode2 against the closed form

Each typical subject is solved without random effects and compared with the
analytic one-compartment solution: a 24-h CsA infusion, an oral PHB dose and a
1-h VAN infusion.

```{r closed-form}
dose_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~amt_mg,    ~dur_h, ~cmt,
  "CsA", 12 * 12.9,  24,     "central",
  "PHB", 20 * 3.3,   0,      "depot",
  "VAN", 15 * 3.2,   1,      "central"
)
grids <- list(
  CsA = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(24, 72, by = 0.25)))),
  PHB = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.01), seq(1, 120, by = 0.5)))),
  VAN = seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.0025)
)
make_typ_events <- function(drug, id) {
  d <- dose_tab[dose_tab$drug == drug, ]
  t <- typ[typ$drug == drug, ]
  # dur = 0 is an instantaneous dose
  dose <- data.frame(id = id, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = d$amt_mg, dur = d$dur_h, cmt = d$cmt)
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = grids[[drug]], evid = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs)
  ev$WT <- t$WT
  ev$PAGE <- if (is.na(t$PAGE)) 40 else t$PAGE
  ev$drug <- drug
  ev
}
closed_form <- function(drug, time) {
  d <- dose_tab[dose_tab$drug == drug, ]
  t <- typ[typ$drug == drug, ]
  k <- t$cl / t$v
  if (drug == "PHB") {
    ka <- exp(th$PHB[["lka"]])
    f <- exp(th$PHB[["lfdepot"]])
    return(f * d$amt_mg * ka / (t$v * (ka - k)) * (exp(-k * time) - exp(-ka * time)))
  }
  r <- d$amt_mg / d$dur_h
  c_end <- r / t$cl * (1 - exp(-k * d$dur_h))
  conc <- ifelse(time <= d$dur_h, r / t$cl * (1 - exp(-k * time)),
                 c_end * exp(-k * (time - d$dur_h)))
  if (drug == "CsA") conc * 1000 else conc
}

typ_sim <- lapply(c(CsA = "CsA", PHB = "PHB", VAN = "VAN"), function(drug) {
  ev <- make_typ_events(drug, 1L)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui[[drug]]), events = ev, keep = "drug",
                       rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
    as.data.frame()
  s$Cc_cf <- closed_form(drug, s$time)
  s
})
cf_err <- vapply(typ_sim, function(s) {
  ok <- s$Cc_cf > 1e-6 * max(s$Cc_cf)
  max(abs(s$Cc[ok] / s$Cc_cf[ok] - 1))
}, numeric(1))
print(signif(cf_err, 3))
stopifnot(all(cf_err < 1e-5))
```

# PKNCA validation

Single-dose NCA of the three typical-subject profiles above, compared with
the analytic AUC (`F * Dose / CL`), the analytic half-life (`log(2) * Vd / CL`)
and the analytic Cmax. The paper reports no NCA, so the reference is the
model's own closed form: this checks the encoding, not the paper's claims.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(typ_sim) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, drug)
dose_df <- dose_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, time = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt = amt_mg, drug)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | drug + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | drug + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

f_oral <- c(CsA = 1, PHB = exp(th$PHB[["lfdepot"]]), VAN = 1)
conc_scale <- c(CsA = 1000, PHB = 1, VAN = 1)
reference <- typ |>
  dplyr::left_join(dose_tab, by = "drug") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    aucinf.obs = conc_scale[drug] * f_oral[drug] * amt_mg / cl,
    half.life = thalf_h,
    cmax = vapply(drug, function(d) max(typ_sim[[d]]$Cc_cf), numeric(1))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(drug, cmax, aucinf.obs, half.life)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = reference,
  by = "drug",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL (CsA); mg/L", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL (CsA); mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "PKNCA on the typical-subject solve against the closed form. * differs by >20%.")

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(drug, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(reference, by = "drug", suffix = c("_nca", "_ref"))
stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_wide) == 3L,
  max(abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs_nca / nca_wide$aucinf.obs_ref - 1)) < 0.01,
  max(abs(nca_wide$half.life_nca / nca_wide$half.life_ref - 1)) < 0.01
)
```

# Replicate Figure 3 (visual predictive checks)

Back 2019 does not report individual doses, so the regimens below are
assumptions (listed under Assumptions and deviations). Figure 3 plots the
natural log of concentration against time after the previous dose; the
observed medians read from it are about ln 7.0 for CsA (1100 ng/mL), ln 3.0 for
PHB (20 mg/L) and ln 2.85 for VAN (17 mg/L). The y-axis unit labels of Figure
3a (ug/mL) and Figure 3c (ng/mL) are swapped relative to these magnitudes.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() seeds R's covariate draws only. rxode2's simulation RNG is
# partitioned per solver thread, so the simulated cohort differs between
# machines with different thread counts; every assertion below is written to
# hold for any cohort.
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
n_arm <- 200L

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(bad <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
  x
}
# Weight and PCA as a Gaussian copula (correlation assumed 0.8), each margin
# log-normal with the Table 1 mean and SD, truncated to the Table 1 range.
copula_cov <- function(n, m_wt, s_wt, r_wt, m_pa, s_pa, r_pa, rho = 0.8) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, 0, 2)
  sl <- function(m, s) sqrt(log(1 + (s / m)^2))
  while (nrow(out) < n) {
    z1 <- rnorm(n)
    z2 <- rho * z1 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(n)
    wt <- m_wt * exp(sl(m_wt, s_wt) * z1 - sl(m_wt, s_wt)^2 / 2)
    pa <- m_pa * exp(sl(m_pa, s_pa) * z2 - sl(m_pa, s_pa)^2 / 2)
    ok <- wt >= r_wt[1] & wt <= r_wt[2] & pa >= r_pa[1] & pa <= r_pa[2]
    out <- rbind(out, cbind(wt[ok], pa[ok]))
  }
  out[seq_len(n), , drop = FALSE]
}

cov_csa <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_arm), WT = rtrunc_norm(n_arm, 12.9, 3.8, 5, 24), PAGE = 40)
m_phb <- copula_cov(n_arm, 3.3, 1, c(1, 6.9), 41.3, 3.9, c(31, 51.1))
cov_phb <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_arm), WT = m_phb[, 1], PAGE = m_phb[, 2])
m_van <- copula_cov(n_arm, 3.2, 2.6, c(0.4, 14.9), 41.2, 14.2, c(25.6, 110))
cov_van <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_arm), WT = m_van[, 1], PAGE = m_van[, 2])

# CsA: two consecutive 24-h infusions (days 1 and 2); observe 14-24 h after
# the start of the day-2 infusion (Figure 3a window).
ev_csa <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cov_csa |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 24)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1, amt = 12 * WT, dur = 24, cmt = "central"),
  cov_csa |> tidyr::crossing(time = 24 + seq(14, 24, by = 0.5)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

# PHB: 20 mg/kg IV loading over 30 min, then 4 mg/kg oral every 24 h from
# 24 h; observe 7.5-25 h after the seventh maintenance dose (Figure 3b).
ev_phb <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cov_phb |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1, amt = 20 * WT, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central"),
  cov_phb |> tidyr::crossing(time = 24 * (1:7)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1, amt = 4 * WT, dur = 0, cmt = "depot"),
  cov_phb |> tidyr::crossing(time = 168 + seq(7.5, 24, by = 0.5)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

# VAN: 15 mg/kg over 1 h every 12 h for 3 days; observe 0.5-12 h after the
# sixth dose (Figure 3c).
ev_van <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cov_van |> tidyr::crossing(time = 12 * (0:5)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1, amt = 15 * WT, dur = 1, cmt = "central"),
  cov_van |> tidyr::crossing(time = 60 + seq(0.5, 12, by = 0.5)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

```{r simulate}
sim_vpc <- function(drug, ev, t_prev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui[[drug]], events = ev, keep = c("WT", "PAGE")) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = drug, tad = time - t_prev)
}
vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_vpc("CsA", ev_csa, 24),
  sim_vpc("PHB", ev_phb, 168),
  sim_vpc("VAN", ev_van, 60)
)
stopifnot(all(c("sim", "Cc") %in% names(vpc)), !anyNA(vpc$Cc))

# Simulated observations are floored at 0.01 mg/L (10 ng/mL for CsA) before
# the log: proportional error can draw non-positive values, and the printed
# vancomycin parameters drive concentrations down to integrator noise, whose
# logarithm is meaningless.
floor_conc <- c(CsA = 10, PHB = 0.01, VAN = 0.01)
vpc_q <- vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(lsim = log(pmax(sim, floor_conc[drug]))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(lsim, 0.05), q50 = quantile(lsim, 0.50),
    q95 = quantile(lsim, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )
pct_floor_van <- 100 * mean(vpc$sim[vpc$drug == "VAN"] < floor_conc[["VAN"]])
observed_median <- data.frame(drug = c("CsA", "PHB", "VAN"), ln_obs = c(7.0, 3.0, 2.85))
```

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(vpc_q, aes(tad, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(data = observed_median, aes(yintercept = ln_obs), linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~drug, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after previous dose (h)",
    y = "ln concentration (CsA ng/mL; PHB, VAN mg/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 3 of Back 2019 under assumed regimens.",
      "Grey: simulated 5th-95th percentile; line: median; red dashed: observed median read from Figure 3.",
      "Simulated values floored at 0.01 mg/L (CsA 10 ng/mL)."
    )
  )
```

```{r vpc-check}
vpc_sum <- vpc_q |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_median = median(q50),
    upper_half = median(q95 - q50),
    fall = q50[which.min(tad)] - q50[which.max(tad)],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(observed_median, by = "drug")
knitr::kable(
  vpc_sum |>
    dplyr::rename("Drug" = drug, "Simulated median (ln)" = sim_median,
                  "Simulated 95th minus median (ln)" = upper_half,
                  "Fall across window (ln)" = fall, "Observed median (ln)" = ln_obs),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Simulated VPC summaries against the observed medians of Figure 3."
)

csa <- vpc_sum[vpc_sum$drug == "CsA", ]
van <- vpc_sum[vpc_sum$drug == "VAN", ]
phb <- vpc_sum[vpc_sum$drug == "PHB", ]
stopifnot(
  # CsA reproduces: the median lands near Figure 3a under the assumed dose,
  # and the upper half-band of IIV plus 46.8% proportional error (expected
  # 0.65 ln units; 0.28 if propSd were ten times smaller, 2.2 if ten times
  # larger) matches the Figure 3a 95th-percentile line, about 0.5-0.7 above
  # the median. The lower half is not used: the floor truncates it.
  abs(csa$sim_median - 7.0) < 0.5,
  csa$upper_half > 0.45, csa$upper_half < 0.9,
  # Known deviation, VAN: the printed CL/Vd put the simulated median several
  # log units below the observed median at any plausible neonatal dose.
  van$sim_median < van$ln_obs - 2,
  pct_floor_van > 50,
  # Known deviation, PHB: the printed Vd makes the profile fall steeply over a
  # window in which Figure 3b is flat.
  phb$fall > 0.5
)
```

The CsA model reproduces its own VPC. The phenobarbital simulated median sits
near the observed level, but the profile falls steeply across the dosing
interval where Figure 3b is flat, and its plotted 5th-95th band is much wider
than the observed one (about ln 2.1 to 3.9). For vancomycin, `r round(pct_floor_van)`% of the simulated
observations 0.5-12 h after the dose are below 0.01 mg/L, so the median sits
on the display floor while the observed median is about 17 mg/L. Both phenobarbital and vancomycin are known
deviations of the published parameter values, recorded in the gate so that a
change to them is noticed. They are not failures of the encoding.

# Errata

Back 2019 has no supplementary material and no NONMEM control stream. No
correction had been registered as of 2026-10-16 (Crossref `update-to` and
`updated-by` empty, Europe PMC `commentCorrectionList` empty, no PubMed
correction link). Table 3 is internally consistent, because every bootstrap
interval brackets its point estimate. The disagreement is between Table 3 and
the paper's own Figure 3. The maintainers encoded Table 3 verbatim and did not
correct either parameter set.

* **Phenobarbital Vd.** CL reproduces the observed level: at the stated
  3-5 mg/kg/day maintenance dose and F = 0.724, the typical-subject average
  steady-state concentration is about 18-30 mg/L, against an observed median of
  about 20 mg/L. However, Vd = 5.51 L at 70 kg is 0.08 L/kg and gives an 11-h
  half-life in the typical neonate. That implies a fall of about two thirds
  over the 7.5-25 h window, where the Figure 3b median is flat. A flat window
  needs Vd of at least about 58 L at 70 kg, roughly ten times the printed
  value, which is consistent with a decimal slip (55.1 printed as 5.51). This
  is an inference and has not been applied.
* **Vancomycin CL and Vd.** The printed values give a typical-neonate CL of
  1.47 L/h/kg, a Vd of 0.046 L/kg and a half-life of 1.3 minutes. The paper
  samples 0.5-23.5 h after the dose, which would be more than 20 half-lives,
  yet Figure 3c shows measurable concentrations across that whole window. The
  chunk below shows that **swapping the CL and Vd rows** of Table 3 (CL 3.23 L/h
  and Vd 69.4 L at 70 kg) gives a typical neonate with CL 0.07 L/h/kg, Vd
  1.0 L/kg and a 10-h half-life. At 15 mg/kg every 12 h, that predicts an
  average concentration close to the observed 17 mg/L. This is shown for
  information only: the swap is a hypothesis about a table-layout error and is
  **not** applied to the model.
* Reading Table 3 as values at the cohort's typical weight rather than at
  70 kg does not rescue the set. It fixes the vancomycin Vd but makes the
  phenobarbital and vancomycin CL tens to hundreds of times too high.

```{r van-swap}
van_t <- typ[typ$drug == "VAN", ]
swap <- tibble::tibble(
  reading = c("Table 3 as printed (encoded)", "CL and Vd rows swapped (not applied)"),
  tvcl = c(69.4, 3.23),
  tvv = c(3.23, 69.4)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl = tvcl * (van_t$WT / 70)^0.75 * van_t$fmat,
    v = tvv * (van_t$WT / 70),
    thalf_h = log(2) * v / cl,
    cavg_15q12 = 30 * van_t$WT / 24 / cl
  )
knitr::kable(
  swap |>
    dplyr::select(reading, cl, v, thalf_h, cavg_15q12) |>
    dplyr::rename("Reading" = reading, "CL (L/h)" = cl, "Vd (L)" = v,
                  "t1/2 (h)" = thalf_h, "Cavg,ss at 15 mg/kg q12h (mg/L)" = cavg_15q12),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical vancomycin neonate (3.2 kg, PCA 41.2 weeks); observed median about 17 mg/L."
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Doses.** No individual doses are reported. The regimens behind Figure 3
  are assumptions. The CsA rate of 12 mg/kg per 24 h was back-calculated by the
  maintainers so that the typical subject sits at the Figure 3a median; the
  paper says only "high dose". PHB uses 20 mg/kg IV loading and 4 mg/kg/day
  oral, the midpoints of the stated ranges. VAN uses 15 mg/kg over 1 h every
  12 h, inside the stated 6-24 h interval range. Only the CsA spread and the
  shape and level contrasts of PHB and VAN are interpreted.
* **Covariates.** Weight and post-conceptional age are drawn as log-normal
  margins with the Table 1 mean and SD, truncated to the Table 1 range, joined
  by an assumed correlation of 0.8; the paper reports no joint distribution.
  CsA has no maturation function, so its cohort carries a placeholder
  `PAGE = 40` that the model does not use.
* **Age variable.** Eq 8 writes the maturation driver as "Age"; Methods
  Eq 2 and Eq 5 define it as post-conceptional age, consistent with TM50 in
  weeks. It is supplied as `PAGE` in weeks.
* **Allometric exponents.** The Discussion says estimated exponents fit the
  infant datasets better than 0.75, but no estimated exponent is tabulated, and
  Eq 7 and Eq 8 print 1 and 0.75. The printed equations govern.
* **TM50 and Hill.** Results 3.3 says both were applied from reference values
  (ref 2, Holford 2013). Table 3 marks only the vancomycin pair as held
  constant; the phenobarbital pair carries RSEs and bootstrap intervals and is
  encoded as estimated.
* **IIV.** Table 3 reports IIV as CV%. The variances use
  `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`. No IIV covariances are reported, and nothing
  printed (no interval on the IIV terms) separates this reading from
  CV = 100 * sqrt(omega). The two readings differ in variance by under 2%
  for both CsA terms and the vancomycin CL, by 8% for the phenobarbital CL,
  13% for the vancomycin Vd and 28% for the phenobarbital Vd (0.482 here
  against 0.619).
* **Residual error.** Concentrations were log-transformed before fitting, and
  Eq 6 writes the constant-CV model as `C = Cpred * (1 + eps)`. The model
  encodes that printed proportional form. For the VPC, simulated observations
  are floored at 0.01 mg/L (10 ng/mL for CsA) before taking logs.
* **Units and specimen.** CsA is returned in ng/mL (doses in mg, volumes in L,
  multiplied by 1000), matching the magnitude of Figure 3a; PHB and VAN are
  returned in mg/L. The Methods call the samples "blood"; Figure 3 labels them
  plasma, and the model files record plasma.
